inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 tanshin (year ended 2026-03-31) cash-flow statement carries no share-based payment line; the only equity award is a director restricted-stock plan settled by disposal of treasury shares (JPY 74m in FY2026, 0.01% of revenue). Treated as SBC-zero; rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.share_count_basis: 61,989,206 issued less 2,840,929 treasury at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin) = 59,148,277; no dilutive securities (diluted EPS reported as '-'). Held flat: SBC is nil and the FY2026 JPY 10.0bn buyback has no announced successor. All history restated for the 1-for-5 consolidation of October 2017.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 2026-06-30: short-term borrowings 44,614 + commercial paper 25,000 + current bonds 10,000 + bonds 10,000 + long-term borrowings 24,758 = 114,372; cash and deposits 48,195. 'Borrowing precious metals' (JPY 52,573m) is a metal-lease liability matched by inventory and is operating, not financial debt: excluded. Lease liabilities are immaterial under J-GAAP (repayments JPY 457m in FY2026) and excluded.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Ordinary-profit basis, which is how DOWA itself reports segment profit: operating profit + depreciation + goodwill amortisation + non-operating items ex interest income and dividend income, with share of profit of equity-method affiliates grossed up to pre-tax at 30% so the 29% cash-tax line returns the after-tax equity income. FY2026: 54,325 ordinary - 324 interest income - 1,492 dividend income + 1,115 interest expense + 30,965 depreciation + 500 goodwill amortisation + 6,554 equity-method gross-up (15,293 x 0.30/0.70) = 91,643 = 12.3% of revenue. FY2025 on the same basis 76,198 = 11.2%. 13-year range of the ungrossed measure 9.5%-12.8%, mean ~11.2%.
inputs.normalized_fcf_note: last_fcf is the reported FY2026 owner FCF (OCF 5,241 - PP&E 34,604 - intangibles 572 = -29,935) and is NOT the projection base; FY2026 OCF carries an 81.4bn inventory build as metal prices rose. The projection is built from components: FY2022-FY2026 average pre-working-capital owner FCF (EBITDA-ord - cash tax - capex) is ~JPY 29.5bn/yr, and the base case settles at JPY 30-39bn/yr from year 6 once the smelter rebuild rolls off.
inputs.equity_method_treatment: Share of profit of equity-method affiliates (JPY 15,293m FY2026, JPY 9,028m FY2025, JPY 6,267m in Q1 FY2027 alone; 94% in the Nonferrous segment, i.e. the Tizapa and Los Gatos zinc/silver mines in Mexico) is kept IN the flows via the EBITDA-ord definition because it is the most commodity-price-sensitive earnings stream and must flex with the scenarios. The matching asset, investments in equity-method affiliates (JPY 32,420m at 2026-03-31, segment note), is therefore NOT added in the bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10-year JGB ~1.7%, Japan ERP 5.5%, beta 1.3 for a metals/smelting cyclical gives cost of equity ~8.9%; after-tax cost of debt ~1.0% (JPY 1,115m interest on ~JPY 100bn average debt, 30% tax); weights ~82/18 at market give ~7.5%. Rounded up to 8.0% to sit near the house JPY industrial reference and because the company is in a capex bulge; NO further cyclical premium and the same WACC in all three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the scenario paths and weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP operating leases are expensed inside EBITDA; lease liabilities (repayments JPY 457m/yr) are immaterial and excluded from net debt. One treatment: operating cost.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; non-controlling interests deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book (JPY 15,368m at 2026-06-30). NCI profit share was JPY 2,037m in FY2026 (3.2% of profit), so book is a fair proxy. FY0 calibration: EBITDA-ord 91,643 - D&A 31,465 = 60,178 EBIT-ord x 0.71 = 42,726 NOPAT vs reported attributable profit 62,458 less ~17bn after-tax extraordinary gains (24,960 Fujita Kanko sale + 3,457 capital-reduction refund - 5,735 extraordinary losses) less 2,037 NCI = ~43.5bn. Ties within non-operating noise.
inputs.working_capital_note: wc_capture -15%: receivables + metal inventories exceed payables and precious-metal borrowings, so revenue growth (which for a smelter is largely metal-price growth) consumes cash and revenue decline releases it. FY2026 realised capture was ~80% of the revenue change because inventory was re-marked with metal prices; -15% is the through-cycle figure, applied symmetrically so the bear case gets the inventory unwind back. Part of the Q1 FY2027 debt increase (JPY 24bn) funded tax and payable settlements rather than inventory, so the overlap with the year-1 WC charge is small (<JPY 100/share) and accepted as conservative.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US cyclical, with the adaptations for JPY WACC, NCI, matching assets and SBC-zero). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. The build deliberately does NOT extrapolate FY2026 (record profit flattered by JPY 28.4bn of extraordinary gains) or FY2027 guidance (JPY 80bn ordinary profit on gold/silver at record highs and JPY 142/USD; the company's own Medium-term Plan 2027 target for the same year is JPY 60bn): year 1 takes guidance with a small haircut for the softening precious-metal prices management flagged at the Q1 release, then revenue mean-reverts (-8%, -5%) and the EBITDA-ord margin settles at 10.5-11.0%, inside the 13-year 9.5-12.8% range. The >JPY 100bn rebuild of the century-old smelting complex (JPY 10bn FY2027, JPY 90bn FY2028-30 per the Analysis) is charged on top of ~JPY 40-45bn/yr ordinary capex, which is why years 2-4 carry 8-8.5% of revenue in capex against ~4% D&A. Price quoted on the TSE in JPY; statements in JPY; no FX. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, so band_position is null by construction. Sanity-check note for the orchestrator: the CSV EBITDA column is operating-profit basis (FY2026 65.2bn); the model's EBITDA-ord (91.6bn) adds equity-method income and other non-operating items, so EV/EBITDA on the CSV basis will read ~1.4x higher than on the model basis.

equity_bridge.item: Available-for-sale investment securities at fair value, after 30% tax on the unrealised gain
equity_bridge.note: Investment securities JPY 88,556m at 2026-06-30 less equity-method investments ~JPY 32,420m (2026-03-31 segment note) = ~JPY 56,136m listed/AFS holdings (largely the residual Fujita Kanko stake and cross-shareholdings). OCI valuation difference JPY 34,049m after tax implies ~JPY 49bn pre-tax unrealised gain; deducting ~JPY 15bn tax gives JPY 41bn. Matching-asset rule: dividend income (JPY 1,492m FY2026) is stripped from the flows.
2026-06-30 balance sheet; flows are consolidated so NCI is charged here, once.
Net retirement benefit liability JPY 21,969m at 2026-06-30 x (1 - 0.30). Service cost is already inside EBITDA; this is the unfunded stock, a debt-like claim.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case mid-cycle nominal growth (JPY inflation ~2% plus modest recycling volume growth); equity CAGR of 9.7-11.4% rejected as cycle-peak-distorted
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 11.4% diverges >30% from revenue 5-yr CAGR 4.9%: FY2026 equity was lifted by JPY 28.4bn of extraordinary gains retained and JPY 14bn of OCI (securities revaluation). Reported EPS CAGRs (35.6%/23.3%) are measured to the FY2026 one-off peak (EPS 1,049.83); on an underlying FY2026 EPS of ~765 (ex after-tax extraordinary gains) they are 22.1%/15.7%, still measured peak-on-trough. Neither is a forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue: FY2021 588.0bn, FY2023 780.1bn, FY2026 745.4bn. Equity attributable: FY2021 265.7bn, FY2023 344.9bn, FY2026 455.6bn. Owner FCF (= reported FCF; SBC nil, interest income not deducted because the company is net debt) is negative at both ends of the 3- and 5-year windows (FY2021 -38.1bn, FY2023 +17.6bn, FY2026 -29.9bn) so a CAGR is undefined; the FY2022-FY2026 average is JPY 12.3bn/yr reported and ~JPY 29.5bn/yr before working capital. Working-capital swings in metal inventory (FY2024 +80.3bn FCF, FY2025 -34.4bn, FY2026 -29.9bn) dominate the reported series.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2027 guidance JPY 941bn (+26.2%; Q1 actual JPY 253.4bn is 27% of it). Y2-Y3 mean-revert metal prices and a firmer yen (-8%, -5%, cumulative -12.6%), leaving FY2029 revenue ~JPY 823bn, above the FY2022-26 average of JPY 750bn because recycling and metal-processing volumes have grown structurally. Then 2-2.5% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 12.5% vs ~13.0% implied by guidance (JPY 80bn ordinary + ~33.5bn D&A + ~9.4bn equity-method gross-up on 941bn) -- the haircut is the softening precious-metal prices, weaker autos and higher material costs management flagged at the Q1 release. Settles at 10.5% by Y3 (FY2022-26 mean on the same basis ~10.9%, 13-year mean ~11.2%) and recovers to 11.0% from Y7 as the rebuilt smelter's productivity gains arrive.
base.capex_rationale: Ordinary capex ~JPY 40-45bn/yr (MTP2027: JPY 100bn business + JPY 45bn ESG investment over FY2025-27; FY2025 actual 47.2bn, FY2026 35.2bn) plus the smelting-complex rebuild of JPY 10bn in FY2027 and JPY 90bn across FY2028-30, giving ~JPY 70bn/yr in Y2-Y4. Reverts to ~4.8% of revenue (capex slightly above D&A) from Y9.
base.tax_rationale: 29% flat: statutory ~30.6%; FY2025 cash rate 29%, Q1 FY2027 book rate 26.7%; FY2026's 16.6% cash rate is timing on the securities-gain tax (payable rose to JPY 11.7bn). The equity-method gross-up in EBITDA-ord means this rate returns the affiliates' after-tax share exactly.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 13x owner FCF for a commodity cyclical with sub-WACC mid-cycle returns (ROE 7.0% FY2025, 5-8% FY2019-21); Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x and is not a multiple a buyer of a Japanese smelter has paid.

bull.narrative: Metals stay structurally elevated and the yen stays weak; margins hold near the FY2027 guided level and then exceed the prior 12.8% peak as the rebuilt smelter and recycling growth compound.

bear.narrative: Precious-metal rally reverses and the yen firms; revenue falls to ~JPY 700bn and margins return to the FY2019-21 trough of 9-9.5% while the rebuild capex is still being spent.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands close to guidance (JPY 941bn sales, ~JPY 80bn ordinary profit) on the strength already banked in Q1 (operating profit JPY 24.7bn exceeded the full H1 target), but gold, silver, copper and zinc then give back part of their 2025-26 run and the yen firms from JPY 142/USD: revenue retraces ~13% over FY2028-29 and the ordinary-basis EBITDA margin settles at 10.5%, roughly the FY2022-26 average, with the Mexican zinc-mine affiliates contributing a mid-cycle ~JPY 9-10bn rather than FY2027's ~JPY 22bn. Environmental Management & Recycling keeps growing on Japan's circular-economy push (segment profit JPY 16.5bn FY2026, up from JPY 6-9bn a decade ago), Metal Processing and Heat Treatment track Japanese auto output, and Electronic Materials stabilises at a low profit without the repeatedly-promised turnaround. The >JPY 100bn smelting-complex rebuild is spent on schedule in FY2028-30, suppressing owner FCF to JPY 1-20bn/yr in those years before it recovers to JPY 30-39bn/yr; the rebuild earns its keep only as a +0.5pp margin lift from year 7. Mid-cycle returns remain a little below the 8% WACC, which is why the value sits below book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold's reserve-asset bid, structural silver and copper deficits and a yen that stays above JPY 140/USD keep metal prices and FX near 2026 levels for several years, so FY2027 guidance is beaten (the Q1 run-rate already implies it) and revenue holds around JPY 950bn-1.0tn rather than retracing. Los Gatos and Tizapa keep paying out at elevated silver and zinc prices. The rebuilt smelter adds critical-minerals capacity and labour productivity, the Kumamoto recycling plant and the Nippon Light Metal battery/solar recycling partnership add volume, and the next-generation silver powder and LED/PD projects finally deliver the Electronic Materials recovery, taking the EBITDA-ord margin past the FY2017 peak of 12.8% to 12.5% sustained on a larger base. Management's MTP2027 ROE >= 10% target is met and exceeded, buybacks continue, and the market pays a 14x FCF exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: The precious-metal rally that management itself flagged as softening at the Q1 FY2027 release reverses in earnest -- gold and silver down 25-30%, zinc and copper down 20% -- while the yen strengthens toward JPY 130/USD. Revenue falls to ~JPY 700bn by FY2029 and the EBITDA-ord margin returns to the 9-9.5% of FY2019-21, when ordinary profit was JPY 24-37bn; equity-method income from the Mexican mines collapses toward the FY2019-20 level. Electronic Materials remains loss-making-adjacent as Chinese silver-powder entrants take share, recycling feedstock competition degrades urban-mining margins, and higher electricity and carbon costs are not passed through. The smelter rebuild is only slightly deferred, so FY2028-30 owner FCF is near zero or negative and the balance sheet absorbs it; the company repeats its MTP2024 miss, and the market caps the exit at 12x a JPY 20bn FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 30/50/20. Bear up because the valuation is being struck with gold and silver at record highs, FY2026 profit flattered by JPY 28bn of one-off gains, FY2027 guidance already above the company's own medium-term target for the same year, and management flagging softening metal prices at the latest release -- mean reversion is the base rate for a commodity price-taker at a cycle peak, and the company has a record of missing its medium-term plans. Bull down because it needs three independent things to hold at once: metal prices and FX staying at 2026 levels, the smelter rebuild delivering, and an Electronic Materials turnaround that has been promised for several plans without arriving.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value DOWA on a mid-cycle owner-FCF stream, not on FY2026's record (one-off-flattered) profit or FY2027's guidance struck at record precious-metal prices. The flows include the Mexican zinc-mine affiliates because they are the most price-sensitive earnings DOWA has; the heavy FY2028-30 smelter rebuild is charged in full with only a modest productivity credit; working capital is tied to the metal-price-driven revenue swings in both directions; and a 13x FCF cap rather than Gordon growth is used for a business whose mid-cycle returns do not clear its cost of capital. The 30/50/20 weighting is the explicit price of buying a cyclical at the top of its price cycle.
key_risks_to_valuation: Metal-price and FX assumption: each 1pp of sustained EBITDA-ord margin is worth roughly JPY 900-1,000/share; the base case's 10.5-11% is a judgment about mid-cycle gold, silver, copper and zinc prices and JPY/USD that may be too low if 2025-26 prices prove structural (bull) or too high if the rally fully reverses (bear).

Smelter rebuild capex: the >JPY 100bn programme is charged on management's FY2028-30 schedule with little growth credited; a deferral, a cost overrun, or a larger-than-assumed capacity/productivity payoff would each move the value by several hundred yen per share.

Equity-method affiliates are valued through their earnings in the flows at consolidated tax rates, not as a separate asset; mine life, Mexican fiscal changes or a sale of the Los Gatos stake would change both the flows and the appropriate treatment.

Working-capital capture of -15% is a through-cycle figure; FY2026 realised ~80% of the revenue change because inventory was re-marked with metal prices, so a continued price rise would consume more cash in year 1 than modelled, and a fall would release more.

AFS securities taken at fair value less tax (JPY 41bn) assume the cross-shareholdings are saleable at book, as the Fujita Kanko sale demonstrated; a market fall in those holdings reduces the bridge directly.
Terminal cap of 13x FCF (12x bear, 14x bull) sets the exit; the Gordon value at 8%/2% would be ~17x and the gap is the price of not assuming a re-rating.
